data.title: DGCA issues show cause notice to SpiceJet over flight cancellations, delays
data.description:
Aviation watchdog DGCA has issued a show cause notice to crisis-hit SpiceJet seeking detailed responses on rising flight cancellations, operational disruptions due to delayed payments and certain violations, according to sources.

The budget carrier, which saw its domestic market share dip to 0.6 per cent in September from 1.2 per cent in August, has been witnessing significant operational issues resulting in flight delays and cancellations.

The Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) has sought explanations from SpiceJet on the continued deterioration in operational performance, reflected in significantly declining OnTime Performance (OTP), increasing flight delays and growing flight cancellations.

In the show cause notice dated November 17, the regulator also flagged the airline's non-adherence to approved schedule, persistent passenger inconvenience arising from flight disruptions, cancellations, delays and inadequate passenger facilitation measures.

 

The airline has been directed to reply within seven days from the date of the issuance of the show cause notice.

"... the majority of the aircraft fleet of SpiceJet is grounded and the airline has failed to submit a credible plan for return to service of the grounded aircraft," the DGCA said in the show cause notice.

Besides, the watchdog has mentioned about uncertainty regarding renewal of mandatory insurance coverage and concerns raised by overseas aviation authorities regarding operational disruptions linked to delayed payments to service providers.

DGCA has also asked an explanation from the airline for non-payment of penalty imposed by it earlier despite repeated reminders.

According to the show cause notice, the airline has failed to comply with eligibility requirements for scheduled international operations and has repeatedly failed to comply with Route Dispersal Guidelines (RDG) despite previous enforcement action and imposition of penalty in May.

Details about the earlier penalty could not be immediately ascertained.

There was no immediate comment from SpiceJet on the show cause notice.

The show cause notice was issued on November 17, a day before SpiceJet's board approved a proposal to raise up to Rs 5,500 crore to shore up its financial position.

Shares of the carrier fell nearly 5 per cent to Rs 9.74 in afternoon trade on the BSE.

BSE has sought a clarification from the airline regarding reports about the DGCA show cause notice.

For the second straight day on Friday, Delhi airport operator DIAL, in a post on X, said that due to operational challenge being faced by SpiceJet, some flights may be impacted.

data.title: PMO adviser flags discom hurdles in expanding India's EV charging network
data.description:
Tarun Kapoor, advisor to the Prime Minister, on Friday flagged lack of cooperation from electricity distribution companies in scaling the electric vehicle charging network in the country.

He also said the government is open to additional funding for the charging infrastructure if required.

"DISCOMs sometimes are not very cooperative," Kapoor said while speaking at the SIAM's first Growth and Readiness for EV Infrastructure Dialogue on Friday.

According to him, distribution companies sometimes demand a substantial amount when setting up charging stations, particularly high capacity ones, and there is a need for a dedicated officer in every distribution company to address this issue.

"The cost of putting up a charging station as you all know the higher part of the cost is behind the metre where sometimes the distribution companies demand a huge amount of money," he said.

 

"Particularly if the charging station needs a higher capacity, say going to 100 KW or more then sometimes they ask for quite a huge amount of money." Kapoor noted that electric vehicles will be an important future source of electricity demand, creating a significant business opportunity for power distribution companies.

"We have been telling DISCOMs that now time has come to realise that EV is going to become one of their largest sectors for power consumption. And as a country we are entering a phase where there is surplus power available," he said.

Kapoor said the government is looking to encourage daytime charging rather than relying completely on overnight charging at homes. Charging facilities should increasingly be located at offices, workplaces, marketplaces and parking areas.

However, low utilisation at some of the existing public charging stations is also a concern, which impacts their maintenance and long-term viability.

Kapoor said some charging stations had utilisation levels of less than 1 per cent, making maintenance difficult for operators.

Adoption of electric vehicles in India is at an early stage, with faster adoption seen in two and three-wheeler segments. Charging infrastructure is one of the key bottlenecks to wider adoption.

Under the Rs 11,900 crore PM E-Drive scheme, the government has set aside Rs 2,000 crore to subsidise charging infrastructure, including up to 72,300 new public EV charging stations, battery swapping stations, and battery charging stations.

"There is a good amount of money available going forward to establish charging infrastructure. And I think the government would be willing to put in more funds also if need be," he added.

data.title: Sensex zooms 1790 pts in 2 days; ₹6.9 trn added to m-cap: 5 key reasons
data.description:
The Indian benchmark indices are on a winning streak as they gained nearly 1 per cent in Friday's intraday session, extending rise to the second day. Meanwhile, they have risen in four of the five trading sessions this week.
 
In intraday deals, 30-pack Sensex added 803 points or 0.97 per cent to hit the day's high of 83,825. In last trade, it gained 990 points, taking the two-day rise to 1,793 points or 2.2 per cent.
 
Similarly, its NSE counterpart Nifty 50 gained 231 points or 0.90 per cent during the day to rise to the day's peak of 25,746. In a span of two days it has gained 518 points or 2.05 per cent.
 
 
During this period, the market capitalisation of BSE-listed stocks has increased by ₹6.90 trillion from ₹506.47 trillion on Wednesday to ₹513.37 trillion today.  
 
Both the benchmark indices are now less than 3 per cent from reclaiming their all-time high levels. The sharp nearly 12 per cent rise seen in November has helped them rebound after a prolonged phase of consolidation.
 

What's driving Indian stock markets?

Here are key factors behind the rise in the Sensex and Nifty today:
 
1. Bank stocks rally
Index-heavyweight banks and financials emerged as the top contributors to the rise seen in the flagship indices today. HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank, Kotak Bank and Axis Bank alone contributed over 500 points or nearly 65 per cent gains seen in the Sensex today.   
ALSO READ: Stock Market LIVE: Sensex jumps 700 pts, Nifty above 25,700; Meesho hits new high
 
The sharp rally in leading private bank stocks has also driven the Nifty Bank above the 64,000 mark for the first time. Data for the first fortnight of November shows that financial services attracted the bulk of the FII inflows at ₹43,102 crore.
 
FIIs are now buying the very same stocks they have been selling to raise money for the AI trade, said Dr VK Vijayakumar, Chief Investment Strategist, Geojit Investment.
 
2. FPI buying
November has seen record buying from foreign investors, with NSDL showing net inflows of 1.14 trillion - the highest ever in a month till date. Strong FPI interest has been a major driver for the Indian equity market, especially as they pivot away from AI-related bets in global markets.
 
"FII buying is so sustained and aggressive that the bulls are calling the shots. Despite occasional dips, the market is likely to remain resilient on the back of massive FII flows assisted by impressive corporate earnings," said Vijayakumar.
 
3. Oil weakness
The oil prices are set for a weekly decline even as they eked out minor gains today. Lower crude oil prices bode well for import-focussed economies like India as it improves the macroeconomic outlook and strengthens the current account deficit.
 
Currently, oil prices are hovering around $92 a barrel, and analysts expect the prices to head lower in the coming year amid supply glut. The IEA's November report puts October supply at 105.4 mb/d and shows observed inventories rising 52 million barrels, the first build since June.
 
Mirae Asset Sharekhan said it expects Brent to end 2027 near $78.
 
4. Earnings growth strong
Elara Capital said that India’s resilient earnings trajectory has been instrumental in anchoring the downside for Indian equities. With earnings revisions gaining positive momentum, even a modest easing of external headwinds could set the stage for a market re-rating, it noted in a note recently.
 
Despite a weaker rupee, a Brent spike above $100/bbl, higher global yields and supply disruptions from the West Asia conflict, the Elara Universe posted robust sales/EBITDA/PAT growth of 23.8%/25.7%/28.7% YoY in Q2FY27. 
ALSO READ: India VIX up 9%, tops 17-mark; analysts say FII flows keep bulls in control
 
5. Technical outlook
Commenting on the technical outlook, SBI Securities said that for Nifty 50, the zone of 25400-25420 will act as a crucial support for the index, while the resistance lies in the zone of 25,710-25,730.
 
In the event of a surge above 25,730, the index can experience an extension of the rally towards 25,800, it opined. On the downside, if the index slips below the level of 25,400, then the next support is placed in the zone of 25,230-25,250. 
ALSO READ: Gold, silver prices fall amid stronger dollar, hawkish Fed signals

data.title: Australia tightens visitor visa rules from November 28: What changes
data.description:
Australia will introduce stricter visitor visa rules from November 28, making the ‘No Further Stay’ condition mandatory across its principal visitor visa categories. "The changes will restrict visitors from applying for another substantive visa while in the country, reinforcing the requirement that visitor visas be used for temporary stays," according to the Migration Amendment (Preventing Further Stay for Visitor Visas) Regulations 2026 introduced on November 13.
 
The condition will apply to all streams of the Visitor visa (subclass 600), the Electronic Travel Authority (ETA, subclass 601) and the eVisitor visa (subclass 651).
 
In practical terms, people travelling to Australia for holidays or to visit family will generally not be able to apply for another visa from within the country to extend their stay or switch to a different visa category.
  
What is Australia's new visa regulation?
 
Under Condition 8503, also known as the ‘No Further Stay’ condition, visa holders are generally prohibited from applying for another substantive visa while in Australia. Exceptions are available for protection visa applications and cases in which immigration authorities grant a waiver.
 
Visitors who wish to extend their stay or change their immigration status will, therefore, generally have to leave Australia and apply for the relevant visa from overseas.
 
Previously, the condition was mandatory for certain visitor visa streams, including the Sponsored Family and Frequent Traveller streams. Immigration authorities could also impose it at their discretion on applicants under most other visitor visa streams, including the Business Visitor stream. ETA and eVisitor holders were exempt from the condition.
 
Australia's Department of Home Affairs may waive the condition in cases involving compelling circumstances that are beyond the visa holder's control and arise after the visa is granted. These may include serious medical conditions, family emergencies or circumstances that prevent a traveller from returning to their home country. 
ALSO READ: H-1B visa workers' children could get Green Card pathway under this US Bill
 
Why has Australia tightened visitor visa rules?
 
The changes are intended to curb visa hopping, a practice in which visitors repeatedly apply for different visas while remaining in Australia, allowing them to extend their stay without leaving the country.
 
The government said the amendments will strengthen visitor visa requirements, support genuine temporary travel and reduce the potential misuse of visitor visas. The changes are also expected to help authorities manage migration levels and net overseas migration.
 
When will the new rules come into force?
 
The regulations will apply to visa applications lodged on or after November 28, 2026. Applications submitted before that date will not be affected.
 
Existing visitor visa holders should check whether condition 8503 has already been attached to their visas, as the new rules do not automatically change the conditions applicable to visas already granted.
 
The amendments do not alter existing visa validity periods or permitted lengths of stay. Eligible ETA and eVisitor holders can continue to make multiple visits to Australia over a 12-month period, generally staying for up to three months on each visit.

data.title: SAHI launches free charting platform with AI-based market analysis tools
data.description:
SAHI, a technology-led stockbroking platform backed by Accel and Elevation Capital, has launched Sahicharts, a browser-based charting platform offering Indian traders and investors free access to market analysis tools.
 
The platform works on desktop and mobile browsers without requiring an app installation. It provides real-time market data for NSE indices, futures and options (F&O) stocks and options.
 
Users can access the platform by signing in with their mobile numbers, without paying subscription fees.
 
Advanced charting tools and real-time market data have traditionally been offered through paid subscriptions. SAHI said Sahicharts was aimed at removing that cost barrier.
 
The company has built the platform in-house using its own chart engine, Flutter and WebSocket technology. It said the platform was optimised for high-speed data processing and smooth chart rendering, and would remain free to users.
 
 
“Indian traders shouldn't have to pay a monthly fee just to see the market clearly,” said Dale Vaz, co-founder and chief executive officer of SAHI.
 
“We built sahicharts.com on our own chart engine so that anyone, whether or not they trade with SAHI, gets real-time NSE charts, AI-based indicators and live scanners for free in their browser. Good tools make for more disciplined trading, and that's what we want to put in every trader's hands,” Vaz said.
 
Sahicharts offers 140 indicators, including 18 AI-based indicators and two community indicators, along with tools for main and sub-charts.
It also provides more than 30 drawing tools that can sync across mobile and desktop.
 
The platform includes 23 real-time market scans, covering categories such as gainers, losers, open interest build-up, daily breakouts, stocks in news and stocks near 52-week highs and lows.
 
These scans cover Nifty indices and all F&O stocks.
 
Manish Jain, co-founder and chief product officer of SAHI, said charting and market intelligence should be integrated into a single workflow.
 
“That’s what we’ve built with SAHI Charts — advanced charting, AI-driven indicators, live scanners and custom tools, all in one place. Traders can explore market movements, analyse different perspectives and build their own trading strategies with greater flexibility,” Jain said.
 
Users can create multiple watchlists, with each capable of holding hundreds of instruments.
The platform also provides a real-time NSE option chain with 24 customisable columns, including open interest, implied volatility and the Greeks.

data.title: Supreme Court upholds Karnataka HC order lifting ban on bike taxis
data.description:
The Supreme Court on Friday dismissed the Karnataka government's appeal against the Karnataka High Court's decision to allow bike taxi services to operate in the state.
 
A Bench of Justices Satish Chandra Sharma and N Kotiswar Singh passed the order, upholding the high court's January 23 judgment that lifted the ban on bike taxis and allowed operators to apply for permits to run the services, Bar and Bench reported.
 

What did the Karnataka High Court ruling say?

 
In its January order, the high court ruled that motorcycles could be registered as transport vehicles and operated as contract carriages under the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988. It held that the state government could impose regulatory conditions but could not refuse permits solely on the ground that the vehicles were two-wheelers.
 
 
A division bench of Chief Justice Vibhu Bakhru and Justice CM Joshi allowed appeals filed by ANI Technologies, which operates Ola, alongside Uber Rapido, motorcycle owners and the Bike Taxi Welfare Association. The appeals challenged an earlier order that barred bike taxi operations until the state framed a policy. 
ALSO READ: UP amends tourism policy to promote budget hotels, homestays and rest stops
 
The high court directed transport authorities to consider applications to register motorcycles as transport vehicles and grant contract carriage permits. It also allowed authorities to impose necessary operational conditions.
 

Why Karnataka govt appealed against the high court order?

 
Karnataka banned bike taxi services in March 2024, citing concerns over passenger safety, alleged misuse of the existing policy and the absence of electric two-wheelers on ride-hailing platforms.
 
The state later challenged the high court's ruling in the Supreme Court, citing passenger safety and insurance coverage concerns. Five auto and taxi driver associations also challenged the decision, arguing that allowing bike taxis without comparable regulatory obligations would adversely affect existing transport operators.
 
Bike taxi services operated by aggregators such as Ola, Uber and Rapido will continue to operate in Karnataka.

data.title: Karthigai Deepam row: SC permits lamp lighting atop Thiruparankundram hill
data.description:
The Supreme Court on Friday allowed the lighting of the Karthigai Deepam lamp atop Thiruparankundram hill on November 24 as a one-time measure.

A bench of Justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul M Pancholi said only authorised persons from Devasthanam (temple administration) and government officials can go for lamp lighting and ordered authorities to deploy necessary security if required.

The top court, however, stayed the Madras High Court judgment allowing the lighting of the traditional Karthigai Deepam lamp atop Thiruparankundram hill.

The Tamil Nadu government had contended on Wednesday that allowing the lighting of the traditional Karthigai Deepam lamp atop the stone pillar near the dargah could lead to thousands of survey pillars across the country acquiring a religious character.

 

The Karthigai Deepam controversy at the Arulmigu Subramaniaswamy temple in Madurai centres on a dispute over where and by whom the lamp should be lit on the Thiruparankundram hill.

For decades, the deepam was lit at the Deepa Mandapam, near the Uchipillaiyar temple on the lower slopes. Hindu groups had sought permission to light the lamp at the Deepathoon, an ancient stone lamp pillar located higher up the hill, approximately 50 metres from the Hazrat Sultan Sikandar Badusha Auliya Dargah.

data.title: RBI clarifies forex reporting rules for services imports and exports
data.description:
The Reserve Bank of India on Friday clarified the scope of foreign ​exchange reporting rules governing services imports ​and exports that went into effect in October ‌and sparked questions about whether they apply to resident individuals.

Earlier this month, the central bank had exempted resident individuals from declaration requirements and introduced a threshold of ₹10 lakh ($10,760.79) for certain reporting obligations.

The RBI on Friday issued a set of frequently asked questions governing services trade transactions. Here are some details:

The central ‌bank clarified that the ₹10 lakh threshold applies to each inward remittance and not the aggregate amount of receipts.

Non-individual service exporters receiving over ₹10 lakh are required to file an export declaration form (EDF) before the credit of proceeds.

 

Authorized banks ​can extend EDF filing deadlines if they consider exporters' reasons to ‌be justified. Banks will be required to publish trade-related policies and key operating procedures ​on ‌their websites.

The RBI notified the original rules governing reporting ‌requirements in January, and they went into effect on October 1.

"These new regulations are designed to ‌align ​with evolving global ​trade practices and aim to significantly enhance the ease of doing business," it said in ‌a Friday ​statement.

data.title: Tata Steel braces for 2030 mine auctions with multi-pronged cost strategy
data.description:
As Tata Steel braces for the auction of its legacy iron ore mines in 2030, it is putting in place a multi-pronged strategy to mitigate a likely rise in raw material costs and preserve its cost competitiveness.
 
T V Narendran, chief executive officer and managing director of Tata Steel, told Business Standard in a recent interview that the company would bid for iron ore mines.
 
“But having captive mines is not an end in itself. The cost economics should be justified,” he said.
 
Pointing out that better-quality iron ore is available outside India at competitive prices, Narendran said Tata Steel could adopt a sourcing strategy similar to the one it follows for coal.
 
“We will find a mix, just like we do in coal. So, there will be an iron ore buying strategy post-2030, which will be a mix of captive plus non-captive, which is what it is for coal,” he said.
 

Four legacy mine leases expire in 2030

 
The need for such a strategy stems from the impending expiry in 2030 of leases for four of Tata Steel's existing iron ore mines — Joda East, Noamundi, Katamati and Khondbond — which currently supply its domestic operations with low-cost iron ore.
 
The lease expiry follows a 2015 amendment to the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Act, which allowed leaseholders of minerals, including iron ore mines used for captive purposes, to continue mining operations until March 31, 2030.
 
In addition to its legacy mines, Tata Steel has expanded its captive mining portfolio through auctions and acquisitions.
 
However, the high premiums commanded by mining blocks in auctions remain a concern for the industry.
 
In 2021, Tata Steel won the Gandhalpada iron ore block in Odisha at a premium of 141.25 per cent.
 
Other mining assets came through acquisitions. Vijaya II was acquired with the Usha Martin steel business, Koida through Neelachal Ispat Nigam Ltd and Kalamang through Bhushan Steel.
 
Tata Steel's FY26 annual report said its India operations had 100 per cent iron ore supply security through captive mines, which produced 44 million tonnes during the year.
 
Its steelmaking capacity in India stood at 27.35 million tonnes in FY26.
 
Apart from developing a new iron ore sourcing strategy, Narendran said the company would continue to take costs out of specific areas.
 
“So that come 2030, we are as good as anyone else, if not better,” he said.
 
Since FY25, Tata Steel has pursued a cost-reduction programme across geographies, driven by initiatives spanning product mix, operational efficiency, procurement, supply-chain management, employee productivity, and leaner practices in stores, repairs and maintenance.
 
Narendran said Tata Steel was also pursuing growth opportunities at locations where it did not carry some of the legacy costs associated with older operations.
 
“We are building capacity at Kalinganagar and Meramandali in Odisha, and later in Maharashtra, where we may not have some of the legacy costs that we have in Jamshedpur,” he said.
 
“We are also closer to the port, at least in the case of Kalinganagar and Meramandali. So, strategically, we are in a much more competitive position, with a largely younger workforce than we have in Jamshedpur. So the cost of labour will be much better,” Narendran added.
 
The company is also working on the revenue side by moving further downstream, getting closer to customers and expanding its business-to-consumer operations.
 
Narendran said these measures were all part of Tata Steel's effort to protect competitiveness when its iron ore costs rise after 2030.
 
“It’s a multi-pronged strategy so that when we hit 2030 and our cost of iron ore goes up, it is mitigated as much as possible through all these initiatives,” he said.
Preparing for 2030 transition
  • Cost takeout in specific areas across geographies
  • Expanding beyond legacy-cost location
  • Focus on downstream, B2C businesses
  • Diversifying iron ore sourcing post-2030: captive and non-captive

data.title: India VIX up 9%, tops 17-mark; analysts say FII flows keep bulls in control
data.description:
India VIX, the volatility gauge of the domestic equity market, climbed nearly 9 per cent on Friday, signalling heightened uncertainty among traders even as benchmark indices extended their gains.
 
As of 1:30 PM, India VIX was up 8.8 per cent at 17.53. The benchmark Nifty 50 rose 185 points, or 0.72 per cent, to 25,700, while the BSE Sensex gained 630 points, or 0.76 per cent, to trade at 83,655.
 
Notably, India VIX has risen for the third consecutive session, gaining over 12 per cent during the period. The rise in volatility has come even as the Nifty 50 advanced more than 300 points, or 1.2 per cent, over the same period.
 
 
India VIX indicates expected volatility in the market over the next 30 days. A sustained rise in India VIX generally indicates increasing expectations of larger market swings and often coincides with cautious investor sentiment. It can also lead to higher option premiums.  Analysts said that the sharp 12 per cent  rise in India VIX over the last three sessions indicates increasing nervousness and uncertainty among market participants, with traders increasingly seeking protection against potential volatility.  "This is particularly significant as the Nifty is trading less than 3% away from its all-time high, suggesting that caution is building despite the broader positive market structure. However, a rise in VIX does not necessarily indicate an imminent correction; rather, it signals expectations of larger market swings over the coming weeks," Sudeep Shah, head - technical and derivatives research at SBI Securities, said. At today's high of 25,745.75, data showed that the Nifty 50 index is less than 3 per cent away from the record high of 26,373.20, touched on January 5, 2026.  READ MORE: Sensex zooms 1790 pts in 2 days; ₹6.9 trn added to m-cap: 5 reasons
 
From a technical perspective, Harish Jujarey, AVP, head - technical equity research, Prithvi Finmart, said that India VIX has moved above its key 50 & 200 - day moving averages, indicating a shift towards a higher volatility moves.  
 
"Going ahead, 18.50 will be an immediate resistance level. A decisive move above this could push India VIX towards the higher range of 27–28, signalling heightened volatility in the equity market," he said. FIIs power market rally 
Analysts said that profit booking is happening in the market but the FII buying is so sustained and aggressive that the bulls are calling the shots. Despite occasional dips, the market is likely to remain resilient on the back of massive FII flows assisted by impressive corporate earnings. 
 
VK Vijayakumar, chief investment strategist, Geojit Investments, said that weakening of the AI trade continues with another 2.25 per cent cut in Nasdaq yesterday, and this is dragging other AI-related markets like South Korea, Taiwan and Japan down. Nifty is the only high performing market in the world this month with a 10.7 per cent surge in just 13 trading days.
 
"It is important to note that the bulk of the FII flows have gone into financial services, particularly the banking majors. FIIs are now buying the very same stocks they have been selling to raise money for the AI trade. Telecom also has been attracting big inflows. The sharp correction in metal prices have attracted buying in auto stocks and consumer durables," he said. FIIs buying this week
 
According to exchange data, foreign institutional investors (FIIs) remained net buyers of Indian equities on all four trading days this week. They purchased shares worth ₹4,864.68 crore on Monday, ₹4,195.38 crore on Tuesday, ₹5,866.78 crore on Wednesday and ₹7,411.41 crore on Thursday. 'Avoid aggressive fresh buying' 
Meanwhile, Sudeep suggested investors to avoid aggressive fresh buying in Nifty at elevated levels, and adopt a staggered investment approach and remain selective, as some consolidation near record highs would be healthy for the market.
 
"Investors should closely monitor Nifty's key support levels, FII activity, global market cues, crude oil prices and overall market breadth. A sustained rise in VIX alongside weakening market breadth and a breach of important support levels could trigger profit booking," he said.
